controls.label: Agent identity verification
controls.description: Can the counterparty verify which agent (software and operator) is acting?

controls.label: Agent registration (know your agent)
controls.description: Must the agent be registered, reviewed or listed before it can transact?

controls.label: User consent capture
controls.description: Is the user's authorization captured in a signed, inspectable artifact?

controls.label: Spending caps
controls.description: Can a maximum amount or budget be bound to the authorization?

controls.label: Merchant or payee scoping
controls.description: Can the authorization be limited to named merchants or payees?

controls.label: Time windows and expiry
controls.description: Do authorizations, tokens or signatures expire by design?

controls.label: Revocation
controls.description: Can the user or operator cancel an authorization before it is used?

controls.label: Step-up authentication
controls.description: Can the flow escalate to the human for a stronger check?

controls.label: Replay protection
controls.description: Are nonces, single-use proofs or time windows enforced against replay?

controls.label: Receipts and evidence
controls.description: Does the flow produce signed receipts or evidence usable later?

controls.label: Dispute support
controls.description: Are chargebacks, refunds or disputes part of the protocol?

controls.label: Reputation
controls.description: Is there a public or shared record of counterparty behavior?

controls.label: Monitoring signals
controls.description: What can a monitor observe to detect abuse while it happens?

controls.label: Kill switch
controls.description: Can an operator stop an agent's ability to transact at once?

cells.note: The on-chain agentId, owner and agentWallet are verifiable, and the optional /.well-known file proves domain control. Nothing proves who operates the agent.
A permissionless registry for discovery: anyone can mint an identity, with no KYC or know-your-agent check.
No consent or mandate object; ERC-8226 (Draft) proposes a mandate layer that can work with ERC-8004 or any other agent registry.
ERC-8004 moves no money, so it has no caps.
agentWallet publishes a payee address that the wallet itself signed for; nothing limits what a client may pay.
Only the wallet-binding signature expires (at most 5 minutes ahead in the reference code).
Clients revoke their own feedback and owners can unset the wallet; an identity cannot be revoked or burned.
Not covered.
EIP-712 domain and deadline bind the wallet signature, but there is no nonce; feedback uses per-client indexes.
proofOfPayment lives in the off-chain feedback file and the file hash is only logged in the NewFeedback event; the registry verifies neither.
Only appendResponse, for example to show a refund; no dispute resolution.
The Reputation Registry: tagged values per client, revocation, responses and a filtered summary.
Public events and tags such as reachable, uptime and responseTime that monitors can publish as feedback.
No pause and no burn; only the registry owner can change the code by upgrade.
Identity is optional and separate from payment: sign-in-with-x (CAIP-122 wallet proof), auth-hints (OAuth 2.0 with DPoP) and RFC 9421 agent signatures in cloudflare:402.
No registry in x402. ERC-8004 can record that an agent accepts x402; cloudflare:402 needs the signature agent registered with Cloudflare.
The protocol has no consent object. The browser paywall asks a human in the UI; agents rely on mandates from other protocols such as AP2.
Budgets are out of scope in the spec. The TypeScript client applies spendControls by default (default assets only, $1 per payment); upto signs a ceiling.
With EIP-3009 and Permit2 the client's signature covers payTo and the amount; with ERC-7710 the delegation's caveats must. EVM upto also names the one facilitator allowed to settle.

validAfter, validBefore, the Permit2 deadline, maxTimeoutSeconds and Lightning invoice expiry bound exact, upto, auth-capture and Lightning authorizations. Batch-settlement vouchers carry no expiry and stay claimable until the escrow is drained; ERC-7710 delegations carry whatever limits the delegator set.

x402 has no revocation message. The signer can race the facilitator by canceling an unused EVM authorization on chain before settlement: EIP-3009 cancelAuthorization (Base USDC implements it), Permit2 nonce invalidation or revoking an ERC-7710 delegation. auth-capture adds void and client reclaim after the capture deadline; batch-settlement channels allow timed withdrawal.

The core specification defines no step-up to the human. The auth-hints extension lets a server require OAuth authentication for specific payment options (a 401 challenge), which identifies the client but is not a risk-based escalation.
Single-use 32-byte nonces enforced by EIP-3009 tokens, Permit2 nonces, cumulative vouchers, and replay stores for Lightning payment hashes.
PAYMENT-RESPONSE carries the transaction hash; the optional offer-receipt extension signs offers and receipts (TypeScript only).

No dispute or chargeback process. exact defines no refund; auth-capture adds void, refund and reclaim, batch-settlement channels refund unclaimed escrow, Solana upto returns unused escrow, and third parties such as x402r add arbitration.
None in x402. ERC-8004 feedback can carry proofOfPayment for an x402 payment.

On-chain settlements (EVM, Solana) are public but look like ordinary transfers; /supported, Bazaar and x402scan expose endpoints and 402 offers. Payment payloads, Lightning payments and cloudflare:402 commitments are not public.
No protocol kill switch. Clients stop by policy or spendControls; servers stop by removing routes; facilitators can refuse to settle.
RFC 9421 signature with a key from the payment scheme's key store; the tag states browse or pay intent.
Agents are onboarded to Visa Intelligent Commerce and approved by the scheme; the process is not public. The Agentic Directory (2026-06-10) lists agents Visa has verified.
Consent lives in VIC, where the user approves each Payment Instruction with a passkey; the ID Token can carry auth_time and amr.
No amounts or limits in TAP; VIC Payment Instructions and network controls apply.
@authority binds the signature to one merchant host and @path to a page; the method and body are not bound.
created and expires at most 8 minutes apart; created must be past and expires future.
An expired or missing key blocks verification; no revocation list or key status endpoint is specified.
Step-up verification and Visa Payment Passkeys happen in VIC.
Nonce plus time window, but nonce tracking is optional for the verifier.
TAP defines no receipt; VIC confirmations and commerce signals serve as transaction evidence.
VIC signals support dispute resolution; no agent-specific liability shift is published.
No reputation mechanism for agents; Agent Score rates merchant sites for agent readiness, not agents.
Visa says TAP feeds telemetry into its fraud and risk models; CDNs expose verification results to zone owners.
Visa can remove a key from its store and merchants can block untagged or failing requests; no emergency procedure is documented.
Bilateral bearer key plus a recommended detached Signature and Timestamp with algorithms agreed out of band; no agent identity scheme.
No registry in ACP. Each platform runs its own merchant and partner onboarding, such as ChatGPT's approved-partner application.
The buyer confirms in the agent interface (a product feature). The spec captures marketing consents and 3DS results but no signed purchase consent.
allowance.max_amount and currency on every delegated token; Stripe SPT usage_limits.max_amount.
allowance.merchant_id and allowance.checkout_session_id bind the token to one merchant and one session.
allowance.expires_at, session expires_at and the expired status.
No revoke endpoint in ACP; Stripe SPTs can be revoked. Agents can cancel open sessions.
authentication_required status, authentication_metadata, authentication_result, Delegate Authentication (3DS2) and capabilities.interventions.
Mandatory Idempotency-Key on POST since 2026-04-17, one_time allowance, webhook timestamp window; request Timestamp checks only SHOULD.
Order with permalink_url and order_create and order_update webhooks; no signed receipt.
Order adjustments include refund, return and dispute; the merchant handles chargebacks as merchant of record; no dispute protocol.
Nothing in the spec.
risk_signals on complete, RiskSignal entries on Delegate Payment, intent_trace reason codes on cancel, Request-Id.
Merchants can decline any order and agents can cancel sessions; Stripe SPTs can be revoked; no protocol-wide stop.
Platform profile URL in UCP-Agent with RFC 9421 signatures against its keys, or API key, OAuth or mTLS bound to that profile.
Permissionless by design; businesses should keep a registry of pre-approved platforms. No know-your-agent registry.
Buyer places the order in a trusted UI unless AP2 is active; buyer_consent map; AP2 checkout_mandate as signed consent.
No cap field; limits live in AP2 mandates, the credential provider or the platform.
Tokens are handler-specific and some (Adyen) are bound to session and merchant; AP2 mandates bind the merchant-signed checkout.
Checkout expires_at defaults to 6 hours; mandate_expired in the AP2 extension.
Remove keys from the profile; RFC 7009 token revocation required for identity linking; OpenID RISC recommended.
requires_escalation handoff through continue_url; 3DS2 device data collection and challenge actions in the optional authentication extension.
Signed Idempotency-Key with 128-bit entropy, 24 to 48 hour storage and 409 on mismatch; Web Bot Auth shape adds nonce.
Order with permalink_url and a required confirmation email; AP2 mandates kept as JCS-canonical evidence.
Order adjustments can record disputes, refunds and returns; dispute handling stays with the business and PSP.
No reputation mechanism for platforms or businesses.
signals such as dev.ucp.buyer_ip and dev.ucp.user_agent, plus signed order webhooks.
Businesses can refuse platforms, answer 503 or cancel sessions; no protocol-level global stop.
The core payment is pseudonymous with an optional DID source; mppx adds RFC 9421 request attestation for Web Bot Auth and Visa TAP, and the card method allows optional TAP headers.
The core forbids requiring accounts for payment; any know-your-customer step belongs to a method (the stripe method needs Stripe accounts on both sides).
Browser wallets should show the origin and ask for explicit confirmation; SPT creation may prompt 3DS or biometrics. No user mandate object.
Caps come from the rail: the session deposit, SPT usage limits, Tempo access key limits. The core has none.
recipient and realm are bound into the challenge id; SPTs are scoped to the seller networkId; v2 session descriptors must match the payee.
Challenges carry expires, subscriptions subscriptionExpires and SPTs expires_at, but session channels and vouchers never expire.
No core revocation message; subscriptions cancel by method-specific means and a payer can force-close a channel.
Method-specific: Stripe may prompt 3DS while creating an SPT; card methods carry network cryptograms.
Single-use challenge ids and proofs, Idempotency-Key, digest binding, and channel and EIP-712 domain binding in sessions.
Payment-Receipt with a method reference on every paid response; session receipts add spent and acceptedCumulative, plus a final SSE event.
Depends on the rail: card and stripe routes keep chargebacks; Stripe stablecoin payments have no disputes; on-chain charges are final.
No reputation layer; the discovery draft only mentions future on-chain anchoring compatible with ERC-8004.
Public explorer data (MPPscan, Tempo chain) and the Stripe Dashboard for Stripe-settled payments; servers should rate-limit.
No protocol stop; a payer stops signing or force-closes, and an operator revokes keys at the wallet or disables a Stripe account.
The agent proves possession of the key in cnf; who the agent is belongs to the commerce protocol layer.
No registry or know-your-agent step; under the Trusted Agent Provider model verifiers keep their own list of trusted providers.
A non-agentic Trusted Surface shows the Mandate Content and authenticates the user before signing.
payment.amount_range per payment and payment.budget across recurring uses.
checkout.allowed_merchants, checkout.line_items, payment.allowed_payees, payment.allowed_pisps and payment.allowed_payment_instruments.
iat and exp on every mandate, payment.execution_date windows and payment.agent_recurrence frequency.
No mandate revocation in v0.2; only short exp and agent-side mandate management.
v0.2 specifies no step-up; a failed check falls back through unresolved_constraint to a user-approved closed mandate. v0.1 had 3DS2 and OTP challenges.
checkout_hash, transaction_id, sd_hash, cnf and the one-presentation-at-a-time rule; consume-once tracking is left to verifiers.
Signed Payment and Checkout Receipts whose reference is the hash of the closed mandate.
Dispute verification steps are defined; retention, retrieval and adjudication are out of scope.
Not addressed.
risk_data from the Trusted Surface; no event or telemetry format.
Credential Providers, networks or processors may reject overlapping mandates or invalidate tokens; card networks keep their own controls.
Registered agents sign requests with RFC 9421 and the tag Agent-pay-auth; verifiers check against the Mastercard key directory at the CDN or merchant.
Registration, security review, certification and trusted agent lists; Skyfire named as Know Your Agent partner on 2026-09-30.
Consumer authorizes the agent and sets limits; passkeys in regional pilots; Verifiable Intent L2 signed by the user key.
Tokens limited by merchant, amount or time window; Verifiable Intent amount_range and budget constraints.
Merchant-specific tokens; Verifiable Intent allowed_merchants and allowed_payees; Intent API srcDpaId check.
Time-limited tokens, signature created and expires, orderExpiry, Verifiable Intent layer lifetimes (L3 at most one hour).
No public revocation API for agents or tokens; Verifiable Intent 0.1 has no revocation protocol, only JWKS key removal and expiry.
Passkeys at consent; deferred orders escalated to the consumer; 3DS for agentic flows still in development at networks and EMVCo.
Mandatory nonce and short window on signatures; single-use tokens and one-time DTVC; Verifiable Intent nonce, aud and one L3 pair per mandate pair.
Verifiable Intent chain gives dispute evidence; intent records kept as chargeback evidence; no receipt object in the program.
Standard chargeback rights; no agent-specific reason codes or liability shift; Verifiable Intent leaves dispute choreography out of scope.
No public agent reputation score; the probability score rates transactions, not agents.
Agent transactions recognizable to issuers; probability score in US testing from 2026-09-30; Verifiable Intent risk_data at consent.
Issuers keep card-level blocks and declines; no documented control to disable one agent across the network.
